chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
Whoever abandons saying, 'I do not know,' his destruction is met.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of refusing to say 'I do not know' in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) links the verbal admission of ignorance ('La adri') to physical safety, suggesting that intellectual humility prevents the 'wounds' of error and conflict. This maxim underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on avoiding hasty judgment (ghafla) and arrogance (kibr), which are seen as precursors to both spiritual and worldly ruin. By acknowledging limits, one preserves the integrity of their knowledge and avoids the pitfalls of dogmatism.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 85. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:
Whoever abandons saying, “I do not know” meets his destruction.
